html:
Satavahanihara is the map's label, from the turn of the eras to 400 CE, for the Deccan plateau ruled by the Satavahana dynasty. The name comes from an old Prakrit place name for a district in the Satavahana homeland.

The Satavahanas rose after the Maurya Empire broke up, and ruled much of the Deccan from about the 1st century BCE to the early 3rd century CE, with a capital at Pratishthana (Paithan). They used Prakrit on their coins and inscriptions, gave land and villages to Brahmins and to Buddhist monasteries, and supported the carving of Buddhist caves in the Western Ghats. In the east, the Amaravati stupa grew under their rule.

Their long rivals were the Saka Western Satraps of Gujarat. Gautamiputra Satakarni beat them in the early 2nd century. Ports on both coasts traded with Rome. After the dynasty faded in the 200s, its lands passed to the Vakatakas, the Andhra Ikshvakus and others, which is why the later snapshots keep the old label.
